newsitem.title: QATAR: Enron aims for Qatar gas deal in April.
newsitem.headline: Enron aims for Qatar gas deal in April.

text.p: U.S. energy giant Enron Corp hopes to finalise a partnership deal with Qatar to set up a $5 billion liquefied natural gas project in April, an Enron official said on Tuesday.
"A 25-member Enron team will begin the final round of negotiations to finalise the deal next week", said Kelly Kimberly, spokeswoman of the Houston-based company.
Qatar-Enron Marketing Company, as the new venture will be called, is designed to produce five million tonnes a year of LNG mainly targeted at the growing Indian market.

Enron is setting up a 2,500-megawatt power plant in Dabhol in the western Indian state of Maharashtra under a 'build- operate-and transfer' deal with the state, which will consume around half of the Qatari project's output.
The remaining half is expected to be supplied to the state's Gujarat Gas Corporation, with which Enron has signed a memorandum of understanding.

Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry, Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, said on Monday that his country would sign a final joint venture deal with Enron only after the U.S. company presented evidence of a firm sales-and-purchase agreement with potential customers.
A long term SPA is crucial to win finance and ensure the successful implementation of gas projects.
Qatar-Enron project is the tiny oil and gas-rich state's third LNG venture to cash in on its North Field gas reserves -- the largest single reserve in the world.
